text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Multi-region failover job started for service-inference. Trigger: AZ outage in us-east-1. Traffic-shift to us-west-2 initiated, but some routes are failing healthchecks. Impact: elevated 5xx in eu-west-1 and latency spikes for EU customers.

Alice M: Acked. I'm oncall. Taking lead. Looking at traffic-shift job and CDN edge errors now.

Ben K: I'm seeing a spike of 502/503 from proxies in eu-west-1 since 3302467960. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/service-inference/requests?from=3302467900

Charlie S: deploy-bot shows traffic-shift job started at 3302468002 -> jobs/traffic-shift/2026-03-15-3302468002 (canary step 10%). Link: https://ci.redwood/jobs/traffic-shift/2026-03-15
deploy-bot: traffic-shift job update: canary 10% -> 50% -> stuck at 50% due to healthcheck failures in eu-west-1 (backend-unhealthy).

Dina R: @Alice M can you confirm DNS changes? I see some regions still pointing to old loadbalancer IPs.

Alice M: running dig +short for inference.redwood.internal across regions.

Alice M: ```
# us-west-2 resolver
> dig +short inference.redwood.internal @1.1.1.1
10.2.1.45

# eu-west-1 resolver
> dig +short inference.redwood.internal @9.9.9.9
10.2.1.45

# us-east-1 resolver
> dig +short inference.redwood.internal @8.8.8.8
10.3.5.12
```

Evan L: that looks like DNS mismatch — some resolvers still returning the old LB (10.3.5.12) in us-east. Could be stale records on our side or cloud DNS zone replication lag.

Ben K: Also seeing BGP flaps for the prefix announced from the us-east LBs. netops-bot might have logs.

netops-bot: Alert: BGP withdraws detected for prefix 203.0.113.0/24 from us-east edge cluster at 3302468015. Re-advertised 3302468030.

Charlie S: If BGP withdrew and re-advertised, some caches / edge ASes may have picked up different next-hops. That explains intermittent 5xx.

Alice M: Confirmed backend pool for the new target in us-west-2 is healthy. Healthchecks failing originate from eu-west-1 due to connection resets. I'm tailing proxy logs.

Alice M: ```
# tail from proxy-eu-1
[3302468021] ERROR: upstream reset by peer 10.3.5.12:443
[3302468035] WARN: TLS handshake failed from 10.3.5.12
```

Dina R: 10.3.5.12 is the old us-east LB — why are eu-west edges talking to the us-east LB? That's the cross-region routing problem.

Evan L: hypothesis: traffic-shift moved control-plane pointers, but route table for the cross-region interconnect didn't update for a subset of ASes, so some edges still route to us-east. Could be a peering flap.

Alice M: mitigation plan: 1) Pause traffic-shift at 50% 2) Roll back canary to 10% 3) Force DNS TTL flush by bumping record with low TTL (5s) for the next minute 4) Ask NetOps to check BGP sessions and edge peering for eu-west-1 -> us-east routes.

Ben K: Agree. Pausing now. deploy-bot: pause job traffic-shift/2026-03-15-3302468002 — paused by @Alice M at 3302468102.

deploy-bot: traffic-shift paused. Current stable state restored to canary 10%.

netops-bot: Investigating peering: looking at us-east -> eu-west-1 transit logs. Summary: one transit provider had scheduled maintenance (unplanned) causing asymmetric routing for ~6m. Engineers contacted.

Charlie S: While peering is being validated, suggest we roll traffic back to pre-failover endpoints for eu-west-1 and throttle any automatic retries.

Alice M: I've updated route-policy to prefer local egress in eu-west-1 for service-inference and invalidated our internal DNS cache on edge fleet. Commands run: 
```bash
# invalidate caches
curl -X POST "https://edge-api.local/cache/invalidate" -d '{"prefix":"inference.redwood.internal"}'
# bump DNS record
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"inference.redwood.internal","Type":"A","TTL":5,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.2.1.45"}]}}]}'
```

Dina R: NetOps confirmed peering provider restored session at 3302468150. BGP routes stabilized.

Evan L: Re-running synthetic checks from eu-west-1 -> inference: 200 OK from 10.2.1.45, latency normal.

Ben K: Error rate back down to baseline in eu-west-1 (rolled mean 5m).

Alice M: Resuming traffic-shift gradually to 20% and will watch. deploy-bot: resume job -> 20% canary at 3302468205.

deploy-bot: traffic-shift canary advanced: 10% -> 20% -> 40% -> 60% -> 100% completed at 3302468330.

Charlie S: Confirming final state: traffic fully shifted to us-west-2, no ongoing 5xx spikes, BGP stable.

Alice M: Post-incident notes: impact window ~3302467960–3302468150 (~3m). Root cause: transit provider peering disruption + stale DNS entries on subset of resolvers causing asymmetric routing during an automated traffic-shift.

Dina R: Customer impact: small % of EU customers experienced 5xx and elevated latency; no data loss. Will prepare customer-facing timeline.

Evan L: Action items: 1) add a pre-flight BGP/peering check to traffic-shift job 2) reduce internal DNS TTL for sway of canary windows 3) run automation to flush edge caches on failover events.

Alice M: I'm handing off to oncall-sre for monitoring and postmortem writeup. @oncall-sre please take next steps.

oncall-sre: Taking over. I'll create the incident report and assign owners for the action items. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved: incident-3302468000 closed by Alice M at 3302468350.

Alice M: Marking as resolved in channel. Will file postmortem doc and notify support & customers.
